title: Console impersonation & temporal roles: access replay and audit-friendly timeline prototype
creator: Marissa Cheng
description: Prototype UX for ephemeral impersonation and temporal roles in Redwood Console. Goal: allow admins and auditors to replay a user's access history, simulate 'who can' for a point-in-time, and surface temporal role grants and expirations in an audit-friendly timeline integrated with existing workspace/org settings. Focus areas: safe impersonation (audit trail + explicit consent), temporal roles visualization (grants, expirations, delegations), access replay (step-through UI with request context), and gated controls for enterprise compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Design includes explicit consent flow and a one-click audit log link for every impersonation session
Timeline view shows grant/event time, source (role, group, delegated), and expiry with color-coded severity
Access replay can filter by resource, time-range, and show request metadata (route, model, tokens)
Prototype includes edge states: suspended roles, retroactive revocations, and emergency override flows with clear warnings
Hand-off tokens and redlines provided for frontend and backend engineers

decisions: Impersonation sessions are always recorded as immutable audit events and cannot be deleted by workspace admins
Temporal roles will be represented as timeboxed grants attached to principals with an explicit expiry timestamp
Default retention set to 90 days with enterprise option; UI surfaces retention period and link to compliance docs
Access replay will be read-only by default; 'perform-as' mode requires elevated approval and logs a separate audit event
